As we wrap up, if you’ve come this far, you’ve already started the journey the author talks about in *Hoodwinked*. It’s a journey that moves us out of the comfort zone of always being sure, and into a world where questions—yes, even the uncomfortable ones—can actually set us free.
The stories and reflections you’ve heard aren’t here to leave you feeling lost. Instead, they offer a different kind of anchor—one that’s rooted in curiosity, humility, and the courage to keep living with questions.
So here are a few gentle reminders to take with you:
Certainty might feel safe, but it’s curiosity that really helps us grow. Every belief—no matter how close to your heart—deserves a closer look. Authority and tradition can point the way, but your own questions should never be silenced. And when you feel doubt or dissent bubbling up, try seeing them as invitations, not threats—because that’s where deeper understanding begins.
The unknown isn’t some empty void. It’s actually where new meaning starts to take shape.
As you go about your days, notice the little rituals and old stories that guide your choices. Every now and then, ask yourself: “What do I really know? And what am I just repeating?” Let yourself be surprised by how freeing it feels to not have every answer. And when you run into experts, leaders, or even your own inner voice that insists it’s right—pause and ask, “What else could be true?”
Remember, this isn’t about staying stuck in doubt forever. It’s about making room for a gentle, ongoing openness—a willingness to learn, to listen, and to change. Sure, it’s not always easy. Sometimes, it can feel isolating or even a little scary. But you’re not alone. Every person who’s ever grown, created, or discovered something new has walked this path, too.
So, trust yourself enough to question. Trust others enough to really listen. And trust the world enough to let it surprise you. Because honestly, this journey of questioning isn’t a side road—it’s life itself, lived with your eyes and your heart wide open.
